plain_english: Thus, of beings, of consciousness-bodied beings — even of Māyā-difference-made, unity is not hard to effect.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ca sati vastūnāṃ cinmātravapuṣāṃ satām māyānirmitabhedānāmapyekatvamadurghaṭam

plain_english: Therein too, what is reflection's object for the worldly — that same: of the knower whose pith is difference of non-difference-shining form.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi yaḥ parāmarśaviṣayo laukikasya saḥ cidabhedaprathārūpabhedasārasya vedituḥ

plain_english: Activity blocked by this — it should touch no other thought; for on touching another thought, knower-difference follows.
sanskrit_cite: vyāpāro'nena ruddho'sau na vikalpāntaraṃ spṛśet vikalpāntarasaṃsparśe mātṛbhedaprasaṅgataḥ

plain_english: Abiding in that-one-reflection, by one-word-superimposition force — the many too would reach unity — as pot-cloth means.
So there is also another — qualifier-qualified relation, for helping; it serves for knowing.
sanskrit_cite: ityasti tāvadanyaśca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoḥ saṃbandha upakārārthaḥ sa jñātumupayujyate

plain_english: Even in manyness there'd be twoness — from double-reflection birth — as the king's horses, chariots, men.
Reflection 'of king' is one, facing own-generality; the other — 'man,' this, with master-generality-relation.
sanskrit_cite: vimarśo rājña ityekaḥ svasāmānyonmukhaḥ paraḥ svāmisāmānyasaṃbandhasahaḥ puruṣa ityayam

plain_english: 'The king's man' — this, after, in relation's range — is to be thought by this; or the former two to be thought — those three in every way.
sanskrit_cite: rājñaḥ puruṣa ityeṣa paścātsaṃbandhagocaraḥ kalpyo'nenātha vā kalpyau pūrvau te sarvathā trayaḥ

plain_english: Genitive-stated relation, settled in the qualifier — reaching qualified-oneness, yet not abandoning own form.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṣṭhyādivācyaḥ saṃbandho viniviṣṭo viśeṣaṇe viśeṣyaikatvamāpanne svaṃ ca rūpamanujjhati
